name: oritain_statistical_data_scientist
gaps_acknowledged: No isotope, geochemistry or supply-chain provenance experience (bridged via CLR compositional analysis and high-dimensional laboratory measurement work)
Under the stated minimum of 2 years commercial statistical modelling experience (internships plus MSc)
No Azure or commercial cloud model deployment; AWS at basic level only
No MLOps or ML lifecycle tooling experience
VS Code and Conda not evidenced in the profile, so not claimed
key_tailoring_decisions: Led the letter and CV skills block with compositional-data analysis (centred log-ratio, PCA, Ward clustering) as the direct bridge to isotope-ratio and trace-element data, which is the non-obvious match no generic data scientist can claim

Front-loaded statistical rigour from the UK Biobank dissertation (logistic regression vs three tree ensembles, AUC 0.714 to 0.718, near-perfect calibration, doubly robust causal forests, E-values, quantitative bias analysis, NHEFS external validation) rather than product analytics

Promoted the Westlake University multi-omics role into Work Experience to evidence high-dimensional laboratory-generated scientific data, and listed R (tidyverse, ggplot2) alongside Python for a science-led team
Named UFLPA and EUDR after verifying them on oritain.com/platform/platform-overview, and described the Origin Fingerprint using the company's own verified wording
Stated the isotope and commercial-experience gaps outright rather than papering over them
warnings: Posting states a minimum of 2 years commercial experience applying statistical modelling and machine learning; the candidate is below that bar and the letter says so.
The Molecular Dynamics project entry had to be cut from the CV to hold one page; molecular dynamics remains in the skills line and in the cover letter.

The UCL education 'Core areas' line maps module content onto the posting's vocabulary (probability, uncertainty, calibration, dimension reduction) rather than quoting module titles. Defensible in interview, but worth knowing.
